summary: Deploy the new Saleor version so its Django migration creates the customer_note column, then backfill all existing note values into customer_note while both versions are live, and finally retire the old version, achieving zero-downtime migration.
write_consistency: Old version writes to note column via Django save(); new version writes to customer_note column via its updated model. After deploy_new, the backfill stage copies existing note values into customer_note for rows where customer_note is NULL, synchronising the columns before old version retirement. During the overlap, writes to note do not affect customer_note and vice versa, so the most recent write by either version is reflected in its respective column.
revision_notes: Removed the expand stage that added customer_note column; column creation is now handled by the new version's Django migration. Backfill stage moved after deploy_new to avoid conflict with migration and ensure column exists before data copy.

stages.description: Copy existing note values into customer_note for rows where customer_note is NULL.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE note IS NOT NULL AND customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version; after this only the new version serves traffic.
